newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court awards RWE partial damages.
newsitem.headline: German court awards RWE partial damages.

text.p: German diversified utility RWE AG is entitled to partial damages from the state of Rheinland Palatinate over delays to the operation of a nuclear power plant, the Federal Supreme Court ruled on Thursday.
RWE had demanded seven billion marks ($4.4 billion) in damages for its initial investment, lost profits and cost of maintaining the station, at Muelheim Kaerlich, near Koblenz, western Germany.
The court ruled that RWE must be compensated for the building and financing costs of the plant as well as the stoppage of business, although not for the full time of the hold-up.
But the court also decided that the RWE did not have to be compensated for lost profits. The exact level of damages is to be set by a court in Koblenz.
The building of the plant was authorised in 1975, when Chancellor Helmut Kohl was premier of the state.
But in 1988, after only a year of operations, the plant was forced to shut down, because of a mistake in the original authorisation. It has stood idle ever since.
The decision means that German states could now be faced by a flood of regressive claims for damages for other large-scale projects held up, or halted by the approval process.
